text: I must say that not everyone, myself certainly, would have his level of expertise when it comes to AI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we are trying to do is to make it pervasive to bring as broad a segment of our population as possible and tying it to a slightly lower hurdle for them to acquire that confidence, that comfort in using AI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, our journey is about ensuring that everyone gets a stable path, covering a pathway devoid of potholes, bringing hopefully everyone to base camp before we prepare to scale the peak.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Jasmin Lau.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But yes, this is the direction that we are committed towards and we should discuss this further in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: I believe my speech has put forth my concerns about advancing mandatory notification for businesses.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: In practice, AI transformation is often gradual and task-based, with roles evolving through redesign, augmentation and changing workflows over time rather than a single identifiable point of elimination.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: Even in my own company, it starts at 10% of tasks being automated, then 30%.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: And it is merged with another function; then, the scope changes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: Would the Member also agree that if definitions are too rigid, firms may avoid gradual redesign altogether and may instead move towards sharper restructuring exercises, which may ironically worsen outcomes for workers, and another possibility that this might even inadvertently cause slower AI adoption and weaken business competitiveness?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: To the extent that there is a court jurisdiction as was the case in Hangzhou in China, I think that there can be made a point to determine whether something is substantively AI-driven redundancy or not.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I think in practice, it will probably depend on the composition of tasks that are automated as well as things that perhaps when the employer pays a lower effective remuneration for.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: But that is why it is very important for there to be an adjudicative process, as I have pointed out in my speech, for workers to be able to better challenge some of these concerns.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Of course, I acknowledge that some of these things may introduce friction for businesses.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I certainly do not deny there is a trade-off.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: But if we do believe that there is this potential for AI to foster very rapid employment changes, then certainly, I think we should err on the side of caution.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I invite Mr Ng Chee Meng to do your rounding up speech?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: All Members recognise that AI adoption is not optional.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: If Singapore is to stay competitive, both enterprises and workers need to raise AI fluency to seize new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: There is also a clear consensus on the transformative potential of AI and on our collective responsibility to manage its impact on our enterprises and our workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: As Minister Tan See Leng and Minister of State Ms Jasmin Lau have pointed out, left to the market, AI growth may not automatically benefit workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Members like Mr Yip Hon Weng warned about an outcome where some workers gain but others risk falling behind.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I am therefore glad that through this Motion, the Government has affirmed that it will not leave outcomes to chance, but will shape the direction of AI growth deliberately and I look forward to the measures that will be unveiled through the Economic Strategy Review report.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: These are no-regrets moves – practical, grounded and effective.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: They lay the foundation for AI growth that translates into good jobs and better prospects for our workers, guiding how AI is adopted, how work is re-organised and how workers can move through change with support and dignity.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: They need trusted intelligence put directly in their hands, so that they can navigate this transition with clarity, not anxiety.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Ms He Ting Ru highlighted the need for Singapore-specific research so that we know the impact of AI disruption on our more vulnerable workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Alex Yeo pointed out that such intelligence could also help us identify where AI is creating new jobs and new industries so that the Government can move early to incentivise AI startups and enterprises to generate fresh opportunities for our workforce.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Assoc Prof Terence Ho likewise underscored the need to deepen local research on how AI is reshaping work to inform our responses and to position Singapore within global research networks on human AI complementarity.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Working with our tripartite partners, LAB seeks to translate international best practices into insights grounded in Singapore's labour market realities so that researchers, adult learners and human resource practitioners alike can have an earlier, clearer basis to act on AI transformation.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Second, on enabling enterprises to transform with AI.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Mark Lee spoke about enterprises' need to transform to stay competitive, making the important point that enterprise and workforce transformation must move together.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng reinforced this – that the real constraint is not the technology, but workforce readiness, and we must move from AI adoption to AI fluency, with clear accountability for worker outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Gerald Giam had a proposal to support employer-led on-the-job training model so that employers, especially SMEs, are incentivised to train and retain workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I acknowledge and support the objectives behind these proposals.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: It is precisely what our CTCs are doing – supporting firms to embark on transformation through structured projects that embed worker training and outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: What we must now do is to deepen it, scale it and focus our efforts on AI across more businesses and sectors.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Mark Lee called for a clearer enterprise "front door" so firms, especially SMEs, are not slowed down by having to navigate multiple schemes and processes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Third, on enabling workers to seize new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Alex Yeo made the point that equipping our workers requires building capability and confidence at the workplace so learning translates into deeper skills.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong highlighted the importance of providing our workers access to AI tools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Dr Neo Kok Beng suggested that we define competencies for the AI age and validate competencies through certifications.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Vikram Nair also made the point that job redesign if done well is the key to ensure that AI creates opportunities and pathways for our workers to grow.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Dr Hamid Razak spoke for the PMEs, residents and parents carrying this anxiety about AI not just for themselves, but for their children.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Indeed, AI-relevant pathways must be tied to job redesign to provide a smoother transition for our youths and PMEs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Several Members have raised concerns about our young graduates.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Mark Lee, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms He Ting Ru and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim highlighted that fresh graduates face challenges not just in finding good jobs, but in accessing the foundational entry-level roles where they learn to become professionals.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: NTUC supports the Government doing more to provide wage supplements if indeed there are wider signs of labour market weaknesses.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: But should this be done too early or too broad a scale, then, employers may not have the right incentive to pay the full wages.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: This is also why good research and understanding of the labour market is needed.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: My fellow labour Members of Parliament – Mr Desmond Tan, Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari, Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Yeo Wan Ling – spoke up from our unions' perspective.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Their asks – that productivity gains are shared, that workers are supported through transitions and that workers are given a genuine voice in AI adoption – exemplify what the Labour Movement stands for in this renewed tripartism in the AI era.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng called the Government to establish clear conditionalities for our support schemes to ensure that public funding goes towards worker outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling called for AI grants to be tied to mandatory job redesign requirements and productivity gains linked to worker outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Andre Low made a similar point that we need accountability mechanisms to ensure that our investments in AI are ensuring augmentation, not automation.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: In response, Minister of State Ms Jasmin Lau shared that the Government's commitment that where public support is given, the Government will expect companies to make the effort to support worker outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Saktiandi, Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Ms He Ting Ru highlighted how AI can cause an uneven impact on jobs as well as uneven benefits across different worker groups.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Members also highlighted segments of workers who may require additional attention.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: As Mr Saktiandi and Ms He Ting Ru pointed out, caregivers and vulnerable workers may have unequal access to AI tools and training.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Ms He Ting Ru spoke about the need to support women.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Gig and Platform workers, as Ms Yeo explained, must be consulted.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Their lived experience is critical input as work evolves with AVs and AI.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: She also called for clearer visibility on the national AV deployment timeline so platform drivers can plan transitions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I also thank Ms Yeo, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Fadli Fawzi for speaking up for our skilled tradesmen.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Amidst AI disruption, we must do more to equip them in AI fluency and build sustainable and respectable career pathways so that they have better work prospects and wages.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Senior workers, as Mr Desmond Tan spoke passionately on, may face more challenges in keeping up with AI disruption and require dedicated support.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I fully agree with Members that we must be alive to the needs of specific segments of workers mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I echo Mr Saktiandi's call for sound policies to shape the trajectory of our AI growth so it benefits workers and citizens and remains inclusive.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: As Ms Poh Li San rightly reminded us, AI also has the potential to augment our workforce and reduce reliance on foreign labour, unlocking the human bottleneck that constrains many businesses today.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: These are in line with the moves I suggested in this House too.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: These are specific, actionable asks that will make a real difference to blue-collar workers and middle class PMEs alike.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: NTUC’s position is clear – our focus is on ensuring the right support to help workers bounce back.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: NTUC is not wedded to any particular form.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Our shared aim is to make the JSS even better, so we can better support our workers, especially our PMEs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also made the important point that we must rigorously track the speed and effectiveness of our existing measures to support workers who face disruption, especially the financial runway for displaced workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I also thank Mr Sanjeev Tiwari, Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Vikram Nair and Ms He Ting Ru for highlighting the potential of AI to cause harm to our workers, such as how AI may intensify workload and introduce risks of discrimination in employment decisions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Members have also surfaced other ideas to contribute to the Motion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Mr Saktiandi suggested for the Government to be the "first customer" of useful AI tools and solutions to facilitate broad and widespread utilisation of AI.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: He also highlighted the need to calibrate data-sharing frameworks and ethical guardrails.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Ms Poh Li San spoke about ethical use of AI in society, to ensure that it is used as a force for good and not for criminal and harmful exploits.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Ms Eileen Chong and Mr Fadli Fawzi spoke about the need to address the impact of AI use on our students, and the impact it might have on our cultures.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: These important issues deserve separate, careful study and consideration beyond the remit of this Motion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: But I thank Members, everyone, indeed, who have spoken up and contributed to this Motion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I really appreciate the conviction and the commitment expressed for the workers and the enterprises, for us to create the biggest possible pie for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I also want to thank tripartite partners who have been on this journey every step of the way: MOM, SNEF and all our different partners.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: I am deeply appreciative, finally, of Mr Sharael Taha's sharing of his experience with labour movements overseas, and his insight that a lack of tripartite trust in their system prevents innovation and change even when this change is most needed.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Even among our own tripartite partners, when there are different views and priorities, we evolve our conversations.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: We work through differences to find win-win positions that are in the best interest of Singapore and our workers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: It is not about labour versus capital, workers against employers, or one group advancing at the expense of the other.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: AI is fast-evolving and we do not have all the answers today.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Its full impact on jobs and businesses will continue to unfold.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: With this House standing united, I am fully confident that we can strengthen our plans and responses at this stage of the AI-enabled growth.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Together with enabled enterprises, we will forge "Tripartism in the AI-era" for win-win outcomes as we have done before – in Singapore, for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am aware of the work of CTCs, but my proposal goes beyond what the CTCs currently provide.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I note the intent of the OJT and agree with the objectives behind the proposal, and it will be studied, considered in our NTUC's work, even as we chart possibilities in career counselling for the youths, and do possible pathways to innovate with the IHLs in career guidance and matches into internship and other possibilities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I will note the point raised and see if we can fulfil the intent, while maybe have variations on the specific pathways.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I do not see any more hands and indeed, after 24 speeches and over seven and a half hours, let me put the question to the House.
